{{Current events|year=2019|month=04|day=7|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]], [[2019 Western Libya offensive]]
**The [[Government of National Accord]] in [[Tripoli]] formally announces the start of a counteroffensive to reclaim all parts of the capital held by the [[Libyan National Army]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/04/libya-gna-forces-announce-counteroffensive-defend-tripoli-190407121535177.html (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[United States Africa Command]] evacuates a contingent of U.S. troops from Libya due to the unrest. [[India]] also withdraws a contingent of peacekeepers from Tripoli. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/apr/07/libya-us-forces-evacuated-haftar-seeks-military-control (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Libyan Air Force]] jets loyal to [[Khalifa Haftar]] strike GNA positions in Tripoli for first time since the offensive began, including four airstrikes near the [[Bab al-Azizia]] military barracks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security-strike/eastern-libyan-forces-conduct-air-strikes-on-tripoli-as-un-fails-to-reach-truce-idUSKCN1RJ0CU (Reuters)] [https://www.voanews.com/a/un-calls-for-urgent-libya-truce-to-evacuate-civilians-wounded/4865342.html (Voice of America)]
**[[Russia]] blocks a [[United Nations Security Council]] statement calling on Libyan [[Field marshal (Libya)|Field Marshal]] Khalifa Haftar to immediately halt the Libyan National Army's offensive on Tripoli, because it wants the UN statement to also apply to pro-GNA forces, including Islamist militias from [[Misrata]]. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/middle-east/article/3005069/air-strikes-bombard-tripoli-eastern-libyan-forces-attempt (''South China Morning Post'')]
*Two female suicide bombers attack a crowd on the outskirts of [[Maiduguri]], [[Nigeria]], killing three civilians and injuring 33 others. [https://guardian.ng/news/suicide-bomb-attack-kills-three-in-maiduguri/ (''The Guardian.ng'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A major [[power outage]] occurs in [[Sudan]], leaving almost the entire country without electricity amid ongoing anti-government [[Sudanese protests (2018–19)|protests]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2019/04/07/sudan-suffers-total-power-outage-amid-anti-bashir-protests/ (Africanews)]
*One person is killed when his car is hit by more then eighty shoots by the brazilian army after his car was mistaken by another one where it was supposed to be criminals in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. [https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/noticia/2019/04/07/homem-morre-apos-carro-ser-atingido-em-acao-do-exercito-na-zona-oeste-do-rio.ghtml (G1)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Andorran parliamentary election]]
**Andorrans head to the polls to elect the new members of the [[General Council (Andorra)|General Council]] that will choose the new [[Prime Minister of Andorra|Prime Minister]]. The ruling party, [[Democrats for Andorra]], loses the majority in the chamber. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/internacional/20190407/461499938895/andorra-elecciones-democrates-per-andorra-toni-marti-partit-socialdemocrata-xavier-espot-pere-lopez.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
*[[Political appointments by Donald Trump]], [[List of Trump administration dismissals and resignations]]
**[[U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|Homeland Security Secretary]] [[Kirstjen Nielsen]] is leaving the administration.  [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection|Customs and Border Protection]] commissioner [[Kevin McAleenan]] will serve in her stead until a new secretary is confirmed by Congress. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/homeland-security-secretary-kirstjen-nielsen-leaving-trump-administration-amid-surge-of-migrants/2019/04/07/97d20358-597d-11e9-b8e3-b03311fbbbfe_story.html?utm_term=.0e7beeafa83f (''The Washington Post'')]
